Title: Maturation of medial efferent system function in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults, term and premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with contralateral broadband noise
Outcome: contralateral suppression absent at 6000 Hz but present at 1500 and 3000 Hz; premature neonates show suppression or enhancement (immature medial efferent function)
Evidence_Quote: term and premature neonates at three f2 frequencies: 1500, 3000, and 6000 Hz, using fixed primary tone frequency ratio (f2/f1 = 1.2) and level separation (10 dB, L1 > L2)

Title: Forward masking among infant and adult listeners.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: tone-burst probe with broadband noise forward masker
Outcome: infants show more forward masking than adults, especially at short masker-probe intervals; susceptibility nearly mature by 6 months
Evidence_Quote: Listeners detected a repeated 1000-Hz probe, with 16-ms rise time, no steady-state duration, and 16-ms fall time. Unmasked thresholds were determined for one group of listeners who were trained to respond when they heard the probe but not at other times. In the masking conditions, each tone burst was preceded by a 100-ms broadband noise masker at 65 dB SPL.

Title: Cisplatin ototoxicity in developing gerbils.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: young gerbils (first exposed at 2 weeks of age; measured at 6 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: cisplatin dosing (1-3 doses) with DPOAE/ABR monitoring
Outcome: dose-related cisplatin ototoxicity (DPOAE/ABR threshold elevation)
Evidence_Quote: A tendency for a bimodal distribution of DPOAE and ABR responses was also observed in the D1 group, at frequencies below 8 kHz.

Title: Development of human cochlear active mechanism asymmetry: involvement of the medial olivocochlear system?
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: pre-term and full-term neonates (73 ears of 38 pre-term and 11 full-term neonates)
Stimulus_Type: contralateral broad band white noise (TEOAE suppression)
Outcome: contralateral suppression of TEOAEs increases with conceptional age; right-ear advantage emerges after 36 weeks
Evidence_Quote: The continuous contralateral stimulation was a broad band white noise, presented at 70 dB SPL.

Title: Modeling otoacoustic emissions by active nonlinear oscillators.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no participants (modeling study compared with experimental data of neonatal spontaneous and evoked OAEs)
Stimulus_Type: none (theoretical oscillator models of otoacoustic emissions)
Outcome: exponential decay with damping coefficients in the 20-200 Hz range fits OAE data; not compatible with a Van der Pol oscillator
Evidence_Quote: an approximately exponential decay law, with characteristic damping coefficients in the 20-200 Hz range, was found to fit the data

Title: Basic properties of the sound-evoked post-auricular muscle response (PAMR).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: human subjects including very young infants (response reaches adult values by 12 months)
Stimulus_Type: click and tone-burst stimuli (post-auricular muscle response)
Outcome: PAMR obtainable within 20 dB of subjective detection threshold; response spectrum mostly between 25 and 200 Hz
Evidence_Quote: can be evoked with tone-bursts between 500 Hz and 16 kHz

Title: Moderate noise trauma in juvenile cats results in profound cortical topographic map changes in adulthood.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: loud tone exposure (noise trauma)
Outcome: mild to moderate high-frequency hearing loss and profound reorganization of the auditory cortex frequency map in adulthood
Evidence_Quote: exposure of 5-week-old kittens to a loud 6 kHz tone, producing mild to moderate high-frequency hearing loss

Title: The effects of maturation and stimulus parameters on the optimal f(2)/f(1) ratio of the 2f(1)-f(2) distortion product otoacoustic emission in neonates(1).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 105 neonates between 30-42 weeks conceptional age and 40 adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f1 sweep)
Outcome: no neonate-adult difference in optimum f2/f1 ratio; optimum ratio depends on f2 frequency and primary tone level
Evidence_Quote: The adult group was used to investigate the effect of stimulus level on the optimum f(2)/f(1) ratio for f(2) frequencies from 1.7 to 10 kHz.

Title: Maturation of human fetal responses to airborne sound in low- and high-risk fetuses.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: low-risk fetuses at 27, 30, 33, and 36 weeks GA (Study 1); high-risk fetuses at 27, 30, 33 weeks GA (Study 2)
Stimulus_Type: airborne sound trials
Outcome: cardiac acceleration and body movement responses begin at 30 weeks GA; cardiac response threshold decreases from 105-110 dB at 33 weeks to 100-105 dB at 36 weeks
Evidence_Quote: received three sound trials at 90, 100, 105 and 110 dB and three no-stimulus control trials

Title: Infants' sensitivity to broadband noise.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz tone and broadband noise (detection task)
Outcome: unmasked and masked detection thresholds; psychometric functions
Evidence_Quote: Unmasked and masked thresholds for a 1000-Hz tone and for broadband noise were estimated adaptively for infants and adults using an observer-based behavioral procedure.

Title: Gender differences among newborns on a transient otoacoustic emissions test for hearing.
Journal: Journal of music therapy
Target_Age: healthy full-term newborns (38-42 weeks gestation), first 48 hours of life (N = 350)
Stimulus_Type: transient evoked otoacoustic emissions (TEOAE) burst stimulus
Outcome: TEOAE response levels (signal-to-noise ratio) by gender, ear, and frequency
Evidence_Quote: During this test, a sudden burst of sound is presented at between 78 and 83 dB SPL which stimulates the entire basilar membrane.

Title: DPOAE suppression tuning: cochlear immaturity in premature neonates or auditory aging in normal-hearing adults?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: normal-hearing school-aged children and adults; premature neonate STCs from a previous study used for comparison
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (suppression tuning curves)
Outcome: children's STCs comparable to adults and different from neonates at 1500 and 6000 Hz; suppression growth not adultlike in children at 6000 Hz only
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE STCs were recorded at 1500, 3000, and 6000 Hz using optimal parameters in normal-hearing children and adults.

Title: Chronic placental insufficiency has long-term effects on auditory function in the guinea pig.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: guinea pigs (tested at 8 weeks of age)
Stimulus_Type: clicks (33 pps) and tone pips for ABR
Outcome: long-term ABR effects of chronic placental insufficiency
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli consisted of 100 micros clicks, presented at 33 pulses per second (pps) and tone pip stimuli at frequencies of 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 kHz.

Title: Maturation of cochlear nonlinearity as measured by distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression growth in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: normal-hearing adults and children, term-born and premature neonates, children with SNHL
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression growth paradigm (primary tone level pairs)
Outcome: suppression growth slope, asymmetry ratio, and suppression threshold by age
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression growth was measured at two f2 frequencies (1500 and 6000 Hz) and three primary tone levels (55-45, 65-55, and 75-65 dB SPL).

Title: Binaural masking level differences in infants with and without otitis media with effusion.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: infants aged 7-10 months (with and without otitis media with effusion)
Stimulus_Type: Tone signal in narrow-band noise masker (binaural masking level difference)
Outcome: Masked thresholds and binaural masking level differences in OME vs non-OME infants
Evidence_Quote: Subjects were trained to detect a 500 Hz signal (either in or out-of-phase between the ears) against an in-phase, narrow band noise masker centred at 500 Hz.

Title: A longitudinal study of distortion product otoacoustic emission ipsilateral suppression and input/output characteristics in human neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: prematurely born neonates (weekly over 7-8 weeks), term-born neonates, normal-hearing adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) ipsilateral suppression and I/O functions
Outcome: suppression tuning, suppression growth, and I/O characteristics by age group
Evidence_Quote: To study this question, DPOAE suppression and I/O functions for f2 = 6000 Hz were measured in a group of prematurely born neonates at weekly intervals over a period of 7-8-weeks, a group of normal-hearing adults, and during a one-time test session in a group of term-born neonates.

Title: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation in neonatally deafened cats: effects of intensity and stimulating electrode location.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation
Outcome: Spiral ganglion neuron survival vs stimulation intensity and electrode location
Evidence_Quote: The mechanisms underlying this maintenance of spiral ganglion neurons induced by chronic electrical stimulation are uncertain, especially since increased neuronal survival was observed over broader sectors of the ganglion than would be expected to be directly activated by the bipolar electrodes and moderate stimulation intensity (6 dB above electrically evoked auditory brainstem response threshold) used. In this report, data are presented from a second series of neonatally deafened and chronically stimulated cats. The parameters for chronic electrical stimulation were manipulated in two simple ways. First, the intensity of the electrical stimulus was reduced from the earlier study, while the duration of chronic stimualtion periods was increased; and secondly, two different intracochlear positions of stimulating electrodes were employed in different experimental groups. Results indicate that elecrical stimulation of the cochlea at an extremely low intensity (2 dB above electrically evoked auditory brainstem response threshold) is sufficient to at least partially prevent or delay ganglion cell degeneration in the deafened cochlea.

Title: Development of f2/f1 ratio functions in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: pre-term infants, term infants, young adults
Stimulus_Type: distortion product OAEs (f2/f1 ratio functions)
Outcome: optimal f2/f1 ratio and Q3 by age, frequency, and gender
Evidence_Quote: Frequency ratio functions were analyzed at three f2 frequencies--2000, 4000 and 6000 Hz.

Title: Middle ear and cochlear disorders result in different DPOAE growth behaviour: implications for the differentiation of sound conductive and cochlear hearing loss.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2 2.0-8.0 kHz; L2 15-60 dB SPL; f2/f1=1.2)
Outcome: DPOAE growth behaviour differentiates middle-ear from cochlear dysfunction
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE I/O-functions were recorded in a wide primary tone level range at up to 8 f2 frequencies between 2.0 and 8.0 kHz (15 dB SPL < L2< 60 dB SPL; L1=0.46 L2 + 41 dB SPL; f2/f1=1.2) in guinea pigs

Title: Decreased arousals among healthy infants after short-term sleep deprivation.
Journal: Pediatrics
Target_Age: 14 healthy infants, median age 8 weeks (range 6-18 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: white noise of increasing intensity
Outcome: arousal thresholds and sleep characteristics after sleep deprivation
Evidence_Quote: During each nap, the infants were exposed, during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, to white noise of increasing intensity, from 50 dB(A) to 100 dB(A), to determine their arousal thresholds.

Title: Cochlear maturation and otoacoustic emissions in preterm infants: a time-frequency approach.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked otoacoustic emissions (wavelet time-frequency analysis)
Outcome: CEOAE band RMS level and latency vs post-conception age
Evidence_Quote: By means of the WT, CEOAEs were decomposed into 12 frequency bands, spanning the 0.25-6.25 kHz range.

Title: Middle ear development. I: Extra-stapedius response in the neonatal chick.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: chicks, 3 days of age to adult
Stimulus_Type: Sound stimulation for extra-stapedius velocity measurement (0.2-10.0 kHz range stated in abstract)
Outcome: Extra-stapedius velocity/phase responses; low-frequency sensitivity increased by 11 dB with age
Evidence_Quote: The ES velocity and phase responses in the frequency range between 0.2 and 10.0 kHz were measured in animals ranging from 3 days of age to adult.

Title: Prevalence of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) recorded (no applied stimulus)
Outcome: SOAE prevalence 0.64 in neonates vs 0.62 in adults; average SOAE levels 8.5 vs -2.6 dB SPL
Evidence_Quote: The majority of adult SOAEs are between 1.0 and 2.0 kHz, whereas the majority of neonatal SOAEs are between 2.5 and 5.0 kHz. The average SOAE level is -2.6 dB SPL for adults and 8.5 dB SPL for infants.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) suppression in 3-month-old infants: evidence for postnatal maturation of human cochlear function?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: premature neonates, term-born neonates, 3-month-old infants, adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE ipsilateral suppression (f2 = 6000 Hz; L1 = 65, L2 = 55 dB SPL)
Outcome: suppression tuning curve features and suppression growth by age
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression tuning curves (STC) and suppression growth patterns were measured in the three age groups at f2 = 6000 Hz, L1 = 65, L2 = 55 dB SPL, with an f2/f1 of 1.2.

Title: Characteristics of the audio sound generated by ultrasound imaging systems.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no human subjects (water-tank experiment; fetal exposure implication)
Stimulus_Type: medical ultrasound scanner pulses
Outcome: audible sound-pressure level generated by the scanner (model and measurement)
Evidence_Quote: It is shown that a typical ultrasound scanner with a typical spatial-peak pulse-average intensity value at 2 MHz may generate a localized sound-pressure level close to 100 dB relative to 20 microPa in the audible (< 20 kHz) range under laboratory conditions.

Title: Influence of swaddling on sleep and arousal characteristics of healthy infants.
Journal: Pediatrics
Target_Age: 16 healthy infants, median age 10 weeks (range 6-16 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: white noise of increasing intensity
Outcome: arousal thresholds in REM sleep; sleep efficiency (swaddled vs nonswaddled)
Evidence_Quote: In both conditions, the infants were exposed to white noise of increasing intensity, from 50 to 100 dB(A), during rapid eye movement sleep, to determine their arousal thresholds.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions for hearing threshold estimation and differentiation between middle-ear and cochlear disorders in neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: neonates (mean age 3.2 days; follow-up at 4 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: distortion product otoacoustic emissions (extrapolated I/O functions)
Outcome: DPOAE hearing threshold estimation; middle-ear vs cochlear differentiation
Evidence_Quote: DPOAEs were measured in neonates after birth (mean age = 3.2 days) and 4 weeks later (follow-up) at 11 test frequencies between f2 = 1.5 and 8 kHz and compared to that found in normal hearing subjects and cochlear hearing loss patients.

Title: The effect of gender on one-day-old infants' behavior and heart rate responses to music decibel level.
Journal: Journal of music therapy
Stimulus_Type: instrumental lullaby music
Outcome: heart rate and behavior state by loudness level and gender
Evidence_Quote: The music--an excerpt of an instrumental lullaby--was presented via small speakers placed on either side of each subject's head and played at three different loudness levels: 55-60 dB, 65-70 dB, and 75-80 dB.

Title: Effects of aspirin on distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression in human adults: a comparison with neonatal data.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: adults with aspirin-induced OHC dysfunction, subjects with SNHL, term newborns
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) ipsilateral suppression
Outcome: DPOAE suppression patterns compared with neonatal data
Evidence_Quote: In the present study, DPOAE suppression was measured at f2 = 1500 and 6000 Hz from two groups with impaired OHC function in an attempt to model the observed immaturity in neonates: adults with aspirin-induced OHC dysfunction and subjects with sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL).

Title: Maturation of the cortical auditory evoked potential in infants and young children.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 10 newborns (<7 days), 19 toddlers (13-41 months), 20 children (4-6 years), 9 adults (18-45 years)
Stimulus_Type: tones (400 Hz and 3000 Hz) and word token /baed/
Outcome: cortical auditory evoked potential (P1, N1, P2, N2) latency and amplitude by age
Evidence_Quote: CAEPs were obtained in response to low (400 Hz) and high (3000 Hz) tones and to the word token /baed/, all presented at 60 dB HL

Title: A retrospective study of the spectral probability of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions: rise of octave shifted second mode after infancy.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 296 human subjects: neonates, children (5-11 years), adults
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (recorded; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: SOAE frequency distribution peaks by age group
Evidence_Quote: Neonates show a monomodal distribution with a peak at 4 kHz, but both children (5-11 y) and adults show an identical bimodal distribution, with two peaks in an octave distance (1.5 and 3 kHz).

Title: Effect of masker-frequency variability on the detection performance of infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz pure tone signal with two-tone complex and broadband noise maskers
Outcome: masked detection thresholds by masker condition
Evidence_Quote: Listeners detected a 300-ms 1000-Hz pure tone masked by: (1) A random-frequency two-tone complex; (2) a fixed-frequency two-tone complex; or (3) a broadband noise. Maskers repeated at 300-ms intervals throughout testing at 60 dB SPL.

Title: Effects of middle-ear immaturity on distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning in infant ears.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression tuning and I/O functions (middle-ear transmission model)
Outcome: model fit of infant and adult DPOAE I/O functions; suppression tuning after level compensation
Evidence_Quote: Results show that once the immaturity was compensated for by providing infants with a relative increase in primary tone level, DPOAE suppression tuning at f2= 6000 Hz was similar in adults and infants.

Title: Theory of forward and reverse middle-ear transmission applied to otoacoustic emissions in infant and adult ears.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants through 6 months and adults (prior-study data)
Stimulus_Type: DPOAEs and ear-canal reflectance (scattering-matrix model)
Outcome: forward and reverse middle-ear transmittance levels, infant vs adult
Evidence_Quote: In a previous study, distortion product (DP) OAE input/output (I/O) functions were shown to differ at f2 = 6 kHz in adults compared to infants through 6 months of age.

Title: Noise in contemporary neonatal intensive care.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: neonates in two NICUs (sound environment survey)
Stimulus_Type: NICU ambient noise (weekly sound surveys; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: weekly equivalent sound levels (LEQ) and exceedance of AAP/SSG recommendations
Evidence_Quote: Median weekly equivalent sound pressure levels (LEQ) for NICU A ranged from 61 to 63 dB (A weighted), depending on the level of care. NICU B L(EQ) measurements ranged from 55 to 60 dB (A weighted).

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning and acoustic admittance in human infants: birth through 6 months.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression tuning curves; ear-canal admittance/reflectance
Outcome: DPOAE suppression tuning and middle-ear indices vs age
Evidence_Quote: Previous work has reported non-adultlike distortion product otoacoustic emission (DPOAE) suppression in human newborns at f2=6000 Hz, indicating an immaturity in peripheral auditory function.

Title: Ear asymmetries in middle-ear, cochlear, and brainstem responses in human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: otoacoustic emissions and auditory brainstem responses evaluated across frequencies
Outcome: ear asymmetries in OAE SNR, signal and noise, and in ABR
Evidence_Quote: Ear differences in OAE SNR, signal, and noise were evaluated separately and across frequencies (1.5, 2, 3, and 4 kHz), and ABR asymmetries were compared with cochlear asymmetries.

Title: In vivo ultrasonic attenuation slope estimates for detecting cervical ripening in rats: Preliminary results.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: rats (pregnant; cervix studied in vivo and ex vivo)
Stimulus_Type: ultrasound attenuation measurement (spherically focused 33-MHz transducers)
Outcome: ultrasonic attenuation slope estimates for detecting cervical ripening
Evidence_Quote: transducers with 33-MHz center frequencies and with 9-mm focal lengths were used in both the simulations and experiments.

Title: Pure-tone overstimulation protects surviving avian hair cells from acoustic trauma.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: intense pure tones (1.5 kHz, then 2.2 kHz), 124 dB SPL
Outcome: protection of surviving hair cells by priming pure-tone exposure
Evidence_Quote: Chicks were exposed to a pure-tone of 1.5 kHz at 124 dB SPL. Lesion was found in both TM and hair cells, but the area of damage to the TM was much larger than that to the hair cells. Following this exposure, chicks were exposed to a second intense pure-tone at 2.2 kHz 124 dB SPL.

Title: Maturation of the traveling-wave delay in the human cochlea.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: humans, 29 weeks conceptional age to 49 years (227 subjects)
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli in high-pass noise masking (derived-response ABR)
Outcome: maturation of the traveling-wave delay in the human cochlea
Evidence_Quote: The derived response technique was applied to ABRs obtained with click stimuli (presented at a fixed level equal to 60-dB sensation level in normal hearing adults) in the presence of high-pass noise masking (slope 96 dB/oct)

Title: Transient evoked otoacoustic emission latency and estimates of cochlear tuning in preterm neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: preterm neonates (58 ears from 34 preterm neonates)
Stimulus_Type: transient evoked otoacoustic emissions
Outcome: TEOAE latency and cochlear tuning estimates vs postconception age
Evidence_Quote: Asymmetry between right and left ears has been found, with the left ears showing no significant change, whereas in the right ears and in the 1.5-2.5 kHz frequency range only, a slow decrease of latency with postconception age (0.1-0.2 ms/week) was observed.

Title: Effects of maturation on tympanometric wideband acoustic transfer functions in human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: wideband acoustic transfer function measurements (tympanometry)
Outcome: energy reflectance and admittance magnitude vs ear-canal pressure and age
Evidence_Quote: For frequencies from 0.25 to 0.75 kHz there was as much as a 30% change in mean ER and mid |Y| with changes in static ear-canal pressure between 4 and 24 weeks of age. From 0.75 to 2 kHz, the effects of pressure produced a small number of significant differences in ER and mid |Y| with age, suggestive of a developmentally stable frequency range. Between 2 and 6 kHz, there were differential effects of pressure for the youngest infants; negative pressures caused increased ER and mid |Y| and positive pressures caused decreased ER and mid |Y|; the magnitude of this effect decreased with age.

Title: Effects of temporal uncertainty and temporal expectancy on infants' auditory sensitivity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz tone in broadband noise
Outcome: masked tone detection sensitivity with and without acoustic cue
Evidence_Quote: In the present experiment, the effects of temporal uncertainty and temporal expectancy on infants' and adults' detection of a 1 kHz tone in a broadband noise were examined.

Title: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation induces selective survival of spiral ganglion neurons in neonatally deafened cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation; ABR/FFR testing
Outcome: Selective spiral ganglion neuron survival in stimulated cochleas
Evidence_Quote: Profound hearing losses were documented by ABR and FFR (500 Hz) testing. At 9-17 weeks of age, the young deafened cats were unilaterally implanted with a multichannel scala tympani electrode. Six of the animals were chronically stimulated at 6 dB above electrically evoked ABR thresholds for 1 h/day for periods of 1 month or 3 months.

Title: Effects of neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation on the cochlear nucleus in cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation
Outcome: Cochlear nucleus spherical cell density, area and volume after deafening/stimulation
Evidence_Quote: The animals were stimulated daily (starting at 13-18 weeks of age), for a period of one hour, at 6 dB above the electrically evoked auditory brainstem response threshold.

Title: Methods for estimating infant thresholds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz, 16-ms tone bursts (threshold estimation)
Outcome: Threshold estimates compared across adaptive procedures and method of constant stimuli
Evidence_Quote: Detection thresholds for 1000-Hz, 16-ms tone bursts were estimated for 3- and 6-month-old infants and for young adults.

Title: The effect of decibel level of music stimuli and gender on head circumference and physiological responses of premature infants in the NICU.
Journal: Journal of music therapy
Target_Age: premature infants in the NICU (gestational ages 28-33 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: lullaby music and classical music (Mozart)
Outcome: head circumference growth; heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation
Evidence_Quote: One quarter of the males and one quarter of the females listened to music presented at an average of 65 dB, one quarter at an average of 70 dB, one quarter at an average of 75 dB, and one quarter did not listen to any music and served as control subjects.

Title: Effect of age at onset of deafness on binaural sensitivity in electric hearing in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: biphasic electric pulse trains at a stimulation rate of 100 Hz (bilateral cochlear implants)
Outcome: ITD sensitivity retained mainly with adult- or late-childhood-onset deafness; ILD sensitivity present in all subjects
Evidence_Quote: Sensitivity to interaural timing difference (ITD) and interaural level difference (ILD) cues was measured at basal, middle, and apical pitch-matched places of stimulation along the cochlear arrays, using a stimulation rate of 100 Hz.

Title: Rapid development of a sensory attribute in young chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Background tone with frequency changes (habituation/peep-delay paradigm)
Outcome: Consistent frequency-change responses emerge within the first postnatal day
Evidence_Quote: Durations of these delays are used as measures of perceived difference between all possible pairs of five frequencies between 500 and 608 Hz.

Title: Auditory processing during sleep in preterm infants: An event related potential study.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: preterm infants (mean GA 30 weeks; tested at mean post-conceptional age 35 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: pure tones, auditory oddball paradigm
Outcome: auditory event-related potentials during active and quiet sleep
Evidence_Quote: An auditory odd-ball paradigm was used with frequently occurring 'standard' tones at 1000Hz and infrequent 'deviant' tones at 2000Hz.

Title: Neuronal responses in chinchilla auditory cortex after postnatal exposure to frequency-modulated tones.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborn chinchilla pups (exposed 4 weeks, tested at P28)
Stimulus_Type: continuous upward linear FM sweep exposure (0.1-20 kHz)
Outcome: Tonal response latencies increased after exposure; FM direction sensitivity minimally affected, speed selectivity decreased
Evidence_Quote: Newborn chinchilla pups were exposed continuously to an upward linear FM sweep (0.1-20 kHz) at 0.05 kHz/ms for 4 weeks.

Title: Ear and hearing problems in relation to karyotype in children with Turner syndrome.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 60 children with Turner syndrome, age 1.7-21.2 years
Stimulus_Type: audiometric evaluation (hearing thresholds by karyotype)
Outcome: Hearing thresholds about 10-11 dB worse in monosomy 45,X/isochromosome than in mosaicism/structural anomaly groups
Evidence_Quote: Hearing thresholds in general appeared to be about 10-11 dB worse in children with a monosomy 45,X or isochromosome (both have a total deletion of the short (p) arm of the X-chromosome) compared to those having a mosaicism or structural anomaly (partial deletion, or total deletion in only a few cells).

Title: Distortion-product otoacoustic-emission suppression tuning in human infants and adults using absorbed sound power.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression tuning with stimulus and suppressor tones (absorbed sound power)
Outcome: Greatest infant-adult STC difference at a stimulus frequency of 6 kHz; STCs more similar when based on absorbed power level than SPL
Evidence_Quote: The greatest difference in distortion product otoacoustic emission (DPOAE) suppression tuning curves (STCs) in infant and adult ears occurs at a stimulus frequency of 6 kHz.

Title: Six-month-old infants discriminate voicing on the basis of temporal envelope cues (L).
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech tokens /aba/ and /apa/ processed to retain envelope information below 64 Hz
Outcome: Infants attended longer to alternating sequences (voicing discrimination from envelope cues alone)
Evidence_Quote: A Headturn Preference Procedure was used to measure looking times in 6-month-old, normal-hearing infants during presentation of repeating or alternating sequences composed of different tokens of /aba/and /apa/ processed to retain envelope information below 64 Hz while degrading temporal fine structure cues.

Title: The breaking of cochlear scaling symmetry in human newborns and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE phase recording with swept-tone protocol (octave-wide segments)
Outcome: DPOAE phase discontinuity around 1.4 kHz (adults) and 1 kHz (infants); steeper low-frequency phase slope in newborns
Evidence_Quote: In this study, DPOAE phase was recorded with a swept-tone protocol in three, octave-wide segments from 0.5 to 4 kHz.

Title: Frequency shifts with age in click-evoked otoacoustic emissions of preterm infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked otoacoustic emissions (CEOAE)
Outcome: CEOAE spectral components shifted with PMA at 10 Hz/week around 2 kHz and 30 Hz/week around 4.25 kHz
Evidence_Quote: The rate in shift in CEOAE spectral components was found to be frequency dependent, with a mean estimate of 10 Hz/week for frequencies around 2 kHz and 30 Hz/week for frequencies around 4.25 kHz.

Title: Developmental changes in ultrasonic vocalizations by infant Japanese echolocating bats, Pipistrellus abramus.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infant Japanese echolocating bats (Pipistrellus abramus), first post-natal month
Stimulus_Type: ultrasonic vocalizations (recorded, not presented)
Outcome: developmental changes in pup vocalization terminal frequencies
Evidence_Quote: Vocalizations by pups on the day of birth were frequency-modulated ultrasounds from 30.0 ± 4.0 kHz to 19.3 ± 1.9 kHz with multiple harmonics. The terminal frequency of the second harmonic (TF(2)) of pup vocalizations corresponded to that of the fundamental (TF(1)) in adult bats (41.4 ± 2.6 kHz), suggesting that pup vocalizations can be easily detected by the mother.

Title: Increased heating by diagnostic ultrasound due to nonlinear propagation.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 3.6-MHz focused ultrasonic beams
Outcome: temperature rise in tissue-mimicking gel (enhancement up to a factor of 3; max 2 degrees C)
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made of the temperature rise in a sample of tissue-mimicking gel, caused by the application of 3.6-MHz focused ultrasonic beams for 3 min.

Title: Processing simultaneous auditory objects: infants' ability to detect mistuning in harmonic complexes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic complex tone (240 Hz) with mistuned third harmonic
Outcome: Infants above chance at 8%, 6% and 4% mistunings; not at 2%
Evidence_Quote: The present study used a conditioned head-turn procedure to examine whether 6-month-old infants are able to discriminate a complex tone (240 Hz, 500 ms, six harmonics in random phase with a 6 dB roll-off per octave) from a version with the third harmonic mistuned.

Title: Infant speech-sound discrimination in noise.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: Speech sounds (/ba/ vs /ga/) in noise at varied signal-to-noise ratios
Outcome: Discrimination performance vs S/N; infant S/N threshold 5.8 dB poorer than adults
Evidence_Quote: Variation in performance as a function of signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) was estimated by testing each infant at four S/N's (-8, 0, 8, and 16 dB).

Title: Postnatal development of 2f1-f2 otoacoustic emissions in pigmented rat.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: distortion-product (2f1-f2) otoacoustic emission primaries
Outcome: functional onset and maturation of 2f1-f2 otoacoustic emissions
Evidence_Quote: The geometric-mean frequencies of the primaries were tested at one-half octave intervals, between 4 and 11.3 kHz. No emissions were detected on postnatal day 12; however, by day 14, emissions were measured at geometric-mean frequencies between 5.7 and 11.3 kHz, but not at 4 kHz. By the 18th postnatal day, all animals had measurable emissions at 4, 5, 7, 8, and 11.3 kHz.

Title: Perception of missing fundamental pitch by 3- and 4-month-old human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: missing-fundamental harmonic complexes; masking noise and pink noise in some experiments
Outcome: Nearly all infants categorized complexes by MF pitch (MF perception by 3 months)
Evidence_Quote: This study investigated the ability of 3- and 4-month-olds to perceive the pitch of MF harmonic complexes based on fundamentals of 160 Hz and 200 Hz using an observer-based method. In experiment I, to demonstrate MF pitch discrimination, 3- and 4-month-olds were required to ignore spectral changes in complexes with the same fundamental and to respond only when the fundamental changed. In experiment II, a 60-260 Hz noise was presented with complexes to mask combination tones at the fundamental frequency. In experiment III, complexes were bandpass filtered with a -12 dB/octave slope to limit use of spectral edge cues and presented with a pink noise to mask all distortion products.

Title: Maturation of the human medial efferent reflex revisited.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: premature and term-born neonates, 6-month-old infants, and young adults
Stimulus_Type: contralateral acoustic stimulation (CAS) during DPOAE recording
Outcome: MOC reflex strongest at frequencies below 1.5 kHz for all ages; maturation likely prior to full-term birth
Evidence_Quote: For all ages, the MOC reflex was strongest at frequencies below 1.5 kHz, and the reflection component of the DPOAE was most affected, showing maximally reduced amplitude and shallower phase slope when contralateral noise was presented.

Title: Development of pitch processing: infants' discrimination of iterated rippled noise stimuli with unresolved spectral content.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: high-pass filtered iterated rippled noise (IRN) stimuli
Outcome: Above-chance discrimination of F0 change from 167 to 200 Hz after pitch priming; performance poor vs resolved stimuli
Evidence_Quote: most 8-month-old infants showed above-chance discrimination of a change from 167 to 200 Hz in the fundamental frequency (F0) of such high-passed filtered IRN stimuli

Title: Perception of the pitch of unresolved harmonics by 3- and 7-month-old human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: missing-fundamental harmonic complexes (unresolved harmonics), bandpass filtered, with pink noise
Outcome: Nearly all infants categorized complexes by MF pitch (discrimination of unresolved harmonics by 3 months)
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli were MF complexes bandpass filtered with a -12 dB/octave slope, combined in random phase, presented at 70 dB sound pressure level (SPL) for 650 ms with a 50 ms rise/fall with a pink noise at 65 dB SPL. The conditions were (1) "LOW" unresolved harmonics (2500-4500 Hz) based on MFs of 160 and 200 Hz and (2) "HIGH" unresolved harmonics (4000-6000 Hz) based on MFs of 190 and 200 Hz.

Title: Preliminary evaluation of a two-interval, two-alternative infant behavioral testing procedure.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 50-dB sound pressure level noise band
Outcome: detection criterion (80% correct) achieved by 10 of 11 infants in a single session
Evidence_Quote: Ten of 11 infants (7-9 months of age) achieved a criterion of 80%-correct detection of a 50-dB sound pressure level noise band in a single testing session.

Title: Distortion-product otoacoustic emission reflection-component delays and cochlear tuning: estimates from across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 184 subjects from prematurely born neonates to elderly adults
Stimulus_Type: distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE at 2f1-f2), reflection component
Outcome: Reflection-component delays estimated across lifespan; term newborns showed longest delays and sharpest tuning
Evidence_Quote: DPOAEs were measured from 0.5-4 kHz in all age groups and extended to 8 kHz in young adults.

Title: Stimulus-frequency otoacoustic emissions in human newborns.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: stimulus-frequency otoacoustic emission (SFOAE) probe tones
Outcome: Neonates had adult-like SFOAE delays when compared at linear-growth stimulus levels
Evidence_Quote: SFOAEs in newborns were measured at stimulus levels as low as 15 dB sound pressure level (SPL). Responses were compared between adults and newborns at stimulus levels where SFOAEs in both age groups demonstrated approximately linear growth (<40 dB SPL for newborns, <25 dB SPL for adults).

Title: Induction of single-sided deafness in the newborn rat and its consequence for cochlear nucleus volume development.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: rats (operated at postnatal day 10; assessed as young adults)
Stimulus_Type: intracochlear neomycin deafening; ABR threshold measurement
Outcome: cochlear nucleus volume development after single-sided deafness
Evidence_Quote: Monaural deafening was considered successful when the hearing threshold was at least 95 dB above the threshold of the normal hearing ear.

Title: Modified spectral tilt affects infants' native-language discrimination of approximants and vowels.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /r/-/l/ and /ɔ/-/ɐ/ with modified spectral tilt (-6 / +6 dB/octave)
Outcome: 6-month-olds discriminated in spectrally modified conditions; 9-month-olds only when unmodified
Evidence_Quote: Infants were presented with /r/-/l/ and /ɔ/-/ɐ/ in three conditions: (a) unmodified; (b) -6 dB/octave tilt; and (c) +6 dB/octave tilt.

Title: Procedures for ambient-pressure and tympanometric tests of aural acoustic reflectance and admittance in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: wideband acoustic reflectance/admittance measurement (ambient pressure and tympanometric)
Outcome: Procedures described; infant absorbance peaks aligned in frequency with group-delay dips (canal-wall mobility model)
Evidence_Quote: Procedures are described to measure acoustic reflectance and admittance in human adult and infant ears at frequencies from 0.2 to 8 kHz.

Title: In vitro ultrasonic heating of fetal bone.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human fetal femurs (in vitro specimens, various gestational ages)
Stimulus_Type: 1 MHz continuous-wave ultrasound exposure (in vitro fetal bone heating)
Outcome: Temperature increase in fetal bone vs soft-tissue absorption values
Evidence_Quote: The temperature increase measured in vitro in human fetal femurs exposed to 1 MHz, continuous wave ultrasound at 37 degrees C is reported.

Title: Heterogeneity of vocal sac inflation patterns in Odorrana tormota plays a role in call diversity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: recorded male calls (audio/video); no presented stimulus
Outcome: Short calls with F0 >5000 Hz inflated pars lateralis only; calls with F0 <4000 Hz inflated pars ventralis only
Evidence_Quote: Short call-types (duration <200 ms) involved inflation of one of the compartments only; those having a fundamental frequency (F0) of >5000 Hz involved inflation of pars lateralis only, whereas those with an F0 of <4000 Hz (tone-pips and "infant" calls) involved inflation of pars ventralis only.

Title: Discrimination of frequency transitions by human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1.0-kHz pulsed-tone standard; linear frequency transitions
Outcome: difference limens for frequency transitions (~3%-4% for 300-ms sweeps; ~6%-7% for 50-ms sweeps)
Evidence_Quote: Difference limens (DLs) for linear frequency transitions using a 1.0-kHz pulsed-tone standard were obtained from 6- to 9-month-old human infants in a series of three experiments.

Title: Recovery of auditory function following intense sound exposure in the neonatal chick.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Intense pure-tone exposure
Outcome: Threshold shift of 60 dB immediately after exposure; near-complete recovery by day 15
Evidence_Quote: One day old chicks were exposed to a 0.9 kHz tone for 48 h at 120 dB. At 0, 1, 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 days after exposure, cochlear nucleus sound-evoked potentials were used to assess threshold sensitivity and frequency selectivity. Immediately after removal from the pure tone a threshold shift of 60 dB relative to age-matched controls was measured.

Title: Developmental changes in masked thresholds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: listeners 6.5 months to 20.5 years of age
Stimulus_Type: Octave-band noises in broadband masker (masked thresholds)
Outcome: Masked thresholds decline exponentially with age
Evidence_Quote: Masked thresholds for octave-band noises with center frequencies of 0.4, 1, 2, 4, and 10 kHz and for a 1/3-octave-band noise centered at 10 kHz were obtained from listeners 6.5 months to 20.5 years of age at two levels of a broadband masker (0 and 10 dB/cycle).

Title: Characterizing spontaneous otoacoustic emissions across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 632 human subjects, premature birth through seventh decade of life
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs); no presented stimulus
Outcome: Newborn SOAEs an average of 5 to 6 dB higher in level, higher-frequency and more numerous than in young adults
Evidence_Quote: Newborn SOAEs are also an average of 5 to 6 dB higher in level than those from young-adult ears.

Title: Phonetic enhancement of Mandarin vowels and tones: Infant-directed speech and Lombard speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 15 Mandarin-speaking mothers interacting with their 12-month-old infants
Stimulus_Type: eight-talker babble noise environment (Lombard speech condition); infant-directed speech
Outcome: Vowel space expansion in IDS and Lombard speech; tone space expansion only in IDS utterance-final position
Evidence_Quote: Vowel and tone productions were produced by 15 Mandarin-speaking mothers during interactions with their 12-month-old infants during a play session (IDS), in conversation with a Mandarin-speaking adult in a 70 dBA eight-talker babble noise environment (Lombard speech), and in a quiet environment (adult-directed speech).

Title: Cortical plasticity with bimodal hearing in children with asymmetric hearing loss.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 10 children with asymmetric hearing loss, implanted at age 8.7 +/- 5.1 years (mean +/- SD)
Stimulus_Type: monaural trains of 9 acoustic clicks/biphasic electric pulses at a rate of 250 Hz, repeated at 1 Hz
Outcome: Cochlear implant use reversed abnormal ipsilateral lateralization and aural preference; resolution limited in children with longer asymmetric hearing duration
Evidence_Quote: Monaurally presented stimuli consisted of 36 ms trains of 9 acoustic clicks/biphasic electric pulses at a rate of 250 Hz, repeated at 1 Hz.

Title: Fetal auditory evoked responses to onset of amplitude modulated sounds. A fetal magnetoencephalography (fMEG) study.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: fetuses at 31 to 40 weeks of gestation (55 pregnant women)
Stimulus_Type: amplitude modulated tone (500 Hz carrier) presented to maternal abdomen
Outcome: Response latencies decreased for middle/high modulation rates vs low; maturation effect observed for 4/s only
Evidence_Quote: Fetal MEG was recorded during the presentation of an amplitude modulated tone (AM) with a carrier frequency of 500 Hz to the maternal abdomen modulated by low modulation rates (MRs) - 2/s and 4/s, middle MR - 8/s and high MRs - 27/s, 42/s, 78/s and 91/s.

Title: Music reduces pain perception in healthy newborns: A comparison between different music tracks and recoded heartbeat.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: 80 healthy full-term newborns aged 1 to 3 days
Stimulus_Type: music tracks (Mozart, Beethoven) and heartbeat sound recordings
Outcome: Music/heartbeat groups showed reduced heart rate and pain perception and increased oxygen saturation vs control
Evidence_Quote: Prospective study of 80 full-term newborns, aged 1 to 3 days, randomly allocated to exposure to Mozart's Sonata for two pianos K.448, Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata, heartbeat sound recordings (70 bpm) or no music.

Title: Ontogeny of auditory brainstem responses in the bat, Phyllostomus discolor.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: juvenile (p7 to p200) and adult bats, Phyllostomus discolor
Stimulus_Type: clicks and narrowband tone pips (ABR audiometry)
Outcome: Tone-pip audiograms responsive from p7 up to 90 kHz; hearing sensitivity increases until about p14
Evidence_Quote: Here we measured auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) to clicks and narrowband tone pips covering a large frequency range (5-90 kHz) in juveniles (p7 to p200) and adults of the bat, Phyllostomus discolor. Tone-pip audiograms show that juveniles at p7 are already quite responsive, not only below 20 kHz but up to 90 kHz.

Title: Amplitude modulation detection and temporal modulation cutoff frequency in normal hearing infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated broadband noise
Outcome: Mean MDT approximately 10 dB poorer in infants; temporal modulation cutoff frequency did not differ between age groups
Evidence_Quote: The modulation detection threshold (MDT) of a broadband noise amplitude modulated at 10 Hz estimated the y-intercept of the TMTF. The cutoff frequency of the TMTF, measured at a modulation depth 4 dB greater than the MDT, provided an estimate of temporal resolution. MDT was obtained in 27 of 33 infants while both MDT and cutoff frequency was obtained in 15 infants and in 16 of 16 adults. Mean MDT was approximately 10 dB poorer in infants compared to adults.

Title: Pure-tone sensitivity of human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones presented monaurally via earphone
Outcome: Infant pure-tone thresholds 10-30 dB higher than adults, greatest difference at 8000 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Pure-tone thresholds at frequencies ranging from 250 to 8000 Hz were estimated for 3-, 6-, and 12-month-old infants and for adults, using the Observer-based Psychoacoustic Procedure (OPP).

Title: Yes/no and two-interval forced-choice tasks with listener-based vs observer-based responses.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz FM tone; word in two-talker speech masking
Outcome: detection thresholds (higher for observer-based than listener-based procedures)
Evidence_Quote: Detection thresholds were estimated adaptively for a 1000-Hz FM tone in quiet and for a word presented in two-talker speech masking.

Title: The influence of developmental noise exposure on the temporal processing of acoustical signals in the auditory cortex of rats.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: Long Evans rats (exposed at P14; recorded at ~6 months and ~2 years)
Stimulus_Type: broad-band noise, 125 dB SPL, 12 min (single exposure at P14)
Outcome: temporal processing of AM noise, FM tones and click trains in auditory cortex
Evidence_Quote: The animals were exposed on postnatal day 14 (P14) for 12 minutes to a loud (125 dB SPL) broad-band noise.

Title: Context matters: Cortical rhythms in infants across baseline and play.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Stimulus_Type: audiovisual display (baseline) and object play with parent; EEG recording
Outcome: Theta/alpha power higher during play; beta/gamma power higher during baseline at frontal sites
Evidence_Quote: Theta (3-6 Hz) and alpha (6-9 Hz) power were higher at frontal sites (Fp1/Fp2) during play relative to baseline. Beta (9-30 Hz) and gamma (30-50 Hz) power were higher at frontal (Fp1/Fp2) and frontal medial sites (F3/F4) during baseline relative to play.

Title: Hearing loss caused by CMV infection is correlated with reduced endocochlear potentials caused by strial damage in murine models.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: mice (inoculated with murine CMV at P3; tested at 6-8 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: tonal stimuli for ABR threshold measurement (8, 16, 32 kHz)
Outcome: CMV-induced strial damage, reduced endocochlear potential and ABR threshold elevation
Evidence_Quote: At 6 weeks, ABR thresholds to tonal stimuli at 8, 16 and 32 kHz were determined for each ear.

Title: The maturation of the central auditory conduction in preterm infants until three months post term. II. The auditory brainstem responses (ABRs).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 65 preterm infants (serial recordings up to three months post term)
Stimulus_Type: auditory brainstem response (ABR) test stimuli at 70 dB
Outcome: ABR component detectability at 70 dB reached 80-100% at about 32 weeks conceptional age; thresholds decreased with age
Evidence_Quote: The detectability of the different components in the ABR tests at 70 dB reached 80-100% at about 32 weeks CA.

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: wave V tuning curves.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: third-octave-filtered click probes with simultaneous tonal maskers (ABR wave V tuning curves)
Outcome: Infant and adult tuning curves similar for the 1.0-kHz probe; infant high-frequency tuning broader (smaller tip-to-tail difference, lower Q10)
Evidence_Quote: Probe stimuli were 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0-kHz third-octave-filtered clicks.

Title: Acoustic analyses of infant fricative and trill vocalizations.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: infant fricative and trill vocalizations (acoustic analysis; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: Infant fricative spectral components at and above 14 kHz; trill rate 16-180 Hz (mean about 100 Hz), about four times the adult rate
Evidence_Quote: Compared to similar fricative sounds in adult speech, the fricative sounds of the 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-month-old infants had primary spectral components at higher frequencies, i.e., to and above 14 kHz. Trill rate varied from 16-180 Hz with a mean of about 100, approximately four times the mean trill rate reported for adult talkers.

Title: Postnatal development of auditory nerve and cochlear nucleus neuronal responses in kittens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: acoustic stimuli for single-unit recording (auditory nerve and cochlear nucleus)
Outcome: postnatal development of neuronal response properties and thresholds
Evidence_Quote: all neurons exhibit broad bandpass tuning curves, with center frequencies clustering near 1.5 kHz.

Title: Infant speech-sound discrimination testing: effects of stimulus intensity and procedural model on measures of performance.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /ba/ vs /da/ at three intensity levels
Outcome: Discrimination performance changed significantly with stimulus intensity
Evidence_Quote: Performance of infants in a speech-sound discrimination task (/ba/ vs /da/) was measured at three stimulus intensity levels (50, 60, and 70 dB SPL) using the operant head-turn procedure.

Title: Level and age effects in infant frequency discrimination.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones
Outcome: Infant FDLs worse than adults' and increased with frequency; FDLs increased at lower sensation level
Evidence_Quote: Frequency difference limens (FDLs) were estimated for 3-, 6-, and 12-month-old infants and for adults using pure tones at 500, 1000, and 4000 Hz. Each listener provided an FDL at 40 dB and at a higher (80 dB, in most cases) sensation level (SL).

Title: Effects of an enhanced acoustic environment on residual hearing following chronic cochlear implantation and electrical stimulation in the partially deafened cat.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: cats (neonatal aminoglycoside-induced partial hearing loss model)
Stimulus_Type: enhanced acoustic environment (80 dB SPL 4-talker babble, 14 h/day); chronic electrical stimulation via cochlear implant
Outcome: effect of enhanced acoustic environment on residual hearing after cochlear implantation
Evidence_Quote: enhanced acoustic environment consisting of 80 dB SPL 4-talker babble presented 14

Title: Infants' localization of sounds in the median sagittal plane: effects of signal frequency.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: bandpass noise bursts (low-pass less than 4 kHz, 4-8 kHz, 8-12 kHz)
Outcome: MAA decreased with age; best performance for the highest-frequency band (8-12 kHz); low-pass signal not reliably localized
Evidence_Quote: For each of three bandpass noise conditions (less than 4 kHz, 4-8 kHz, 8-12 kHz), minimum audible angle (MAA) for each listener, i.e., the smallest of the four angular shifts in vertical sound location that the listener could reliably detect, was estimated.

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: restriction of frequency contribution by notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli with simultaneous notched-noise maskers (notch centers 1.0, 4.0, 8.0 kHz)
Outcome: Wave V latency/amplitude similar for adults and infants within the 1.0-kHz notch; group differences at higher notch frequencies
Evidence_Quote: Notch center frequencies were set at 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0 kHz. Responses were obtained at 20, 40, and 60 dBnHL during the simultaneous presentation of each notched-noise masker as well as in an unmasked condition.

Title: Neural processing of auditory temporal modulations in awake infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: awake infants 3- and 10-month-olds and awake young adults
Stimulus_Type: amplitude-modulated stimuli (AMFR, slow and faster modulation rates)
Outcome: AMFR at 8 Hz at all ages; reliable 40 Hz responses only in adults
Evidence_Quote: for both slow and faster modulation rates (8 and 40 Hz)

Title: Changes in middle-ear input admittance during postnatal auditory development in chicks.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: middle-ear input admittance measurement at 7 frequencies (0.66-1.8 kHz)
Outcome: postnatal development of middle-ear input admittance
Evidence_Quote: Admittance at 7 frequencies (0.66-1.8 kHz) was calculated from measurements of the magnitude and phase angle of sound pressure in front of the tympanic membrane.

Title: Masking effects on ABR waves I and V in infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 4-kHz tone pip with high-pass and low-pass maskers
Outcome: Masking patterns for ABR waves I and V differed between infants and adults, largest difference for wave I
Evidence_Quote: The signal was a 4-kHz tone pip presented at 86 dB peak equivalent sound-pressure level (p.e.SPL).

Title: Infants' discrimination of final syllable fundamental frequency in multisyllabic stimuli.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: synthetic multisyllabic speech stimuli with final-syllable F0 increments relative to a 150-Hz standard
Outcome: Above-chance discrimination of F0 increments of 5-30 Hz relative to the 150-Hz standard
Evidence_Quote: Discrimination performance was above chance expectation for increments of 10, 20, and 30 Hz relative to a 150-Hz standard.

Title: Infant pitch perception: evidence for responding to pitch categories and the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic tonal complexes signaling two pitch categories (fundamentals 160 and 200 Hz)
Outcome: Infants categorized harmonic complexes by pitch, including complexes with the fundamental removed (missing fundamental)
Evidence_Quote: In the present study 7-8-month-old infants demonstrated the ability to discriminate harmonic complexes from two pitch categories that differed in pitch by approximately 20% (e.g., 160 vs 200 Hz).

Title: Maternal vocalisations and other sounds in the fetal lamb's sound environment.
Journal: Early human development
Stimulus_Type: maternal vocalisations and other sounds recorded inside the amniotic sac (hydrophone); ewe bleat playback
Outcome: Attenuation of external sounds decreased at 500-4000 Hz over the last 3 weeks of gestation; lamb heart-rate responses differed for own mother's vs alien ewe's bleats
Evidence_Quote: Over the last 3 weeks of gestation the attenuation of sounds from outside the mother decreased at frequencies between 500 and 4000 Hz, but not below or above those frequencies.

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human infants: pure-tone masking profiles for clicks and filtered clicks.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click and filtered-click stimuli with simultaneous pure-tone maskers (ABR)
Outcome: ABR wave V latency/amplitude masking profiles; greater low-frequency contribution in infants than adults
Evidence_Quote: Masking profiles at two intensities (60 and 40 dBn HL) were obtained for click, as well as 4000- and 1000-Hz filtered-click stimuli.

Title: Auditory structure and function in the bird middle ear: an evaluation by SEM and capacitive probe.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: five avian species; neonatal chick and parakeet for functional measurements
Stimulus_Type: acoustic stimulation for tympanic membrane velocity/displacement measurement (capacitive probe)
Outcome: TM velocity response resembled a bandpass filter (best frequency 1.5-3.0 kHz); roll-off 6 dB/octave (low) and 16 dB/octave (high); TM displacement linear between 70 and 120 dB SPL
Evidence_Quote: The velocity vs frequency response curve, measured from the tip of the concave tympanic membrane, and corrected to a constant stimulus level of 100 dB SPL, was obtained for the neonatal chick and parakeet for frequencies between 0.2 and 10.0 kHz with a capacitive probe. In both species this curve resembled a bandpass filter whose best frequency was in the range of 1.5-3.0 kHz. The low and high frequency roll-off was 6 and 16 dB per octave, respectively. Displacement of the TM in the chick was measured at several frequencies between 70 and 120 dB SPL and was found to be linear.

Title: TRPA1 deficiency affects cochlear potentials days after noise exposure.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: 8 kHz tone burst (ABR/rCM recording); noise exposure
Outcome: TRPA1-dependent changes in cochlear potentials (SP, rCM) after noise exposure
Evidence_Quote: mice exhibited a direct current (DC) shift in the rCM elicited by an 8 kHz tone burst as the sound intensity increased

Title: Age-dependent effects of a pure tone trauma in the chick basilar papilla: evidence for a development of the tonotopic organization.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: chicks/chick embryos (embryonic day 18 or 20; post-hatching days 1, 10, 20, 30)
Stimulus_Type: pure tone 1.5 kHz at 125 dB SPL, continuous 12 h
Outcome: age-dependent shift of maximum threshold elevation (development of tonotopic organization)
Evidence_Quote: 58 chicks or chick embryos were continuously exposed during 12 h on either embryonic day 18 or 20 or on post-hatching days 1, 10, 20 or 30 to 1.5 kHz pure tone at an intensity of 125 dB SPL. After a 20- or 30-day survival time, audiograms were recorded and then the basilar papillae were prepared for scanning electron microscopy. The frequency of maximum threshold elevation was seen at about 4 kHz when the chicks were exposed to the traumatic tone at embryonic day 18.

Title: Frequency and intensity discrimination in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 26 infants aged 7-9 months and six young adults
Stimulus_Type: ongoing train of 1.0-kHz tone bursts with frequency/intensity increments and decrements
Outcome: Infant frequency DLs 11-29 Hz and intensity DLs 3-12 dB (adult DLs 3-5 Hz and 1-2 dB); no infant discriminated intensity decrements
Evidence_Quote: Subjects were visually reinforced for responding to frequency increments, frequency decrements, intensity increments, or intensity decrements in an ongoing train of 1.0-kHz tone bursts, and stimulus control was monitored using randomly interleaved probe and catch trials.

Title: Early hearing deprivation by silicon earplugs does not alter electrophysiological development of mouse dorsal cochlear nucleus fusiform neurons.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: mice (earplugs inserted at P14; assessed 5-7 days later)
Stimulus_Type: silicon earplugs at P14 (early hearing deprivation)
Outcome: electrophysiological development of dorsal cochlear nucleus fusiform neurons
Evidence_Quote: inserting silicon earplugs at P14, elevating auditory thresholds by 30-40 dB

Title: Binaural interactions in cortical area AI of cats reared with unilateral atresia of the external ear canal.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: adult cats (unilateral atresia of the external ear canal created shortly after birth)
Stimulus_Type: tones delivered to both tympanic membranes via sealed acoustic system
Outcome: binaural interactions in cortical area AI; shift of interaural-intensity-difference sensitivity
Evidence_Quote: The intensity needed for a stimulus to the atretic ear to participate in the binaural response was as much as 50 dB higher than that at the opposite normal ear

Title: Consistency and variability in pitch and tempo in infants' everyday musical lives.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Stimulus_Type: live song renditions (lullaby, pop song)
Outcome: Large individual differences in pitch/tempo consistency across singers
Evidence_Quote: singing a pop song 30 bpm and six semitones apart

Title: Exploring the effect of attention on the acoustic change complex: cross-condition reliability and between-subject variability.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz tone with 10% frequency change (ACC)
Outcome: No attention effect on ACC latencies/amplitudes; good cross-condition reliability
Evidence_Quote: toward 1 kHz sound stimuli containing a 10% frequency change (2000 ms pre-transition duration; 128 trials)

Title: Postpartum survival of mice exposed in utero to ultrasound.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: mice (exposed in utero on gestation Day 8)
Stimulus_Type: continuous-wave ultrasound, 2 MHz, 0.44 W/cm2 spatial average intensity, 60-180 s
Outcome: postpartum survival after in utero ultrasound exposure
Evidence_Quote: mice exposed in utero on Day 8 of gestation to ultrasound at 0.44 W/cm2 (+/- 20%) spatial average intensity, 2 MHz, continuous wave, for 60--180 s in a 37 degrees C water bath.

Title: Frequency and age-dependent auditory evoked potential thresholds in infants.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 40 normal infants 2-28 weeks old and 14 normal hearing adults
Stimulus_Type: tone pips (0.5, 4.0, 10.0 kHz)
Outcome: Infant-adult threshold difference greatest at 4.0 kHz and decreased with age; no significant difference at 500 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Auditory evoked-potential thresholds to 0.5, 4.0 and 10.0 kHz tone pips were measured in 40 normal infants 2-28 wks old and 14 normal hearing adults.

Title: Maturational and degenerative processes in the organ of Corti after neonatal hypothyroidism.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: rats (propylthiouracil during the first 30 days after birth)
Stimulus_Type: BAER and electrocochleography measurement (propylthiouracil-induced neonatal hypothyroidism)
Outcome: maturational and degenerative processes in the organ of Corti; elevated auditory thresholds
Evidence_Quote: Maturation of auditory potentials was achieved within 10-15 days but was incomplete since the animals definitely demonstrated elevated thresholds around 60-70 dB SPL.

Title: Auditory handicap of hearing impairment and the limited benefit of hearing aids.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: none (quantitative model/review of hearing impairment and hearing aids)
Outcome: model of auditory handicap (loss classes A and D); limited hearing-aid benefit
Evidence_Quote: The latter class represents the first stage of auditory handicap, beginning at an average hearing loss of about 24 dB.

Title: Fundamental frequency in the speech of infants and children.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: six normal infants and children from 33 to 169 weeks
Stimulus_Type: infant and child noncry utterances (narrow-band spectrographic analysis; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: Fundamental frequency values ranged from 30 to 2500 Hz; fry, modal, and high registers used
Evidence_Quote: Fundamental frequency values ranged from 30 to 2500 Hz, well outside the values reported in previous studies of noncry utterances.

Title: Infants' discrimination of intensity variation in multisyllabic stimuli.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: synthetic CVC syllable in bisyllabic/trisyllabic context; intensity increments
Outcome: discrimination of intensity increments (above chance at 2 dB; better in bisyllabic than trisyllabic context)
Evidence_Quote: Discrimination performance was above chance for a 2-dB increment, and improved for 4- and 6-dB increments.

Title: Acoustical properties of the human skull.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: axisymmetric focused ultrasound beam through skull specimens
Outcome: insertion loss, reflection loss and sound speed of the human skull
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made in the frequency range from 0.25 to 6 MHz. Most studies were restricted to an upper frequency limit of 2.2 MHz.

Title: An analysis of auditory brainstem responses in infants.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 148 infants from 4 to 60 weeks of age
Stimulus_Type: filtered clicks (1, 2, 4, 8 kHz) and broadband click
Outcome: ABR wave I, III, V latencies decreased with age, largest for wave V and for 1 kHz responses
Evidence_Quote: Filtered clicks of 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz were presented at two intensities, 30 and 50 dB HL re the average threshold for a group of young adults. Responses to a broadband click, 50 dB nHL, were also recorded.

Title: Acoustic features of infant vocalic utterances at 3, 6, and 9 months.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants at 3, 6, and 9 months of age
Stimulus_Type: infant comfort-state vocalizations (acoustic analysis; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: Mean f0 445 Hz at 3 months, 450 Hz at 6 months, 415 Hz at 9 months; F1 and F2 ranges increased with age
Evidence_Quote: The f0 frequency averaged 445 Hz for 3-month-olds, 450 Hz for 6-month-olds, and 415 Hz for 9-month-olds.

Title: Infants' pitch perception: inharmonic tonal complexes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic and inharmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental)
Outcome: infants discriminate and categorize inharmonic complexes by pitch; performance deteriorates for the more strongly inharmonic complexes (30 Hz partial shift)
Evidence_Quote: infants demonstrated the ability to discriminate two harmonic complexes based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: Filtering and spectral characteristics of averaged auditory brain-stem response and background noise in infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts (ABR); 30-Hz vs 100-Hz high-pass recording filters
Outcome: infant ABR energy concentrated below 100 Hz; 30 Hz high-pass filter yields larger-amplitude ABR and better signal-to-noise ratio than 100 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli used to elicit ABRs are moderate- and low-level clicks and 500-Hz tone bursts.

Title: Gap detection in infants, children, and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 500-Hz Gaussian-enveloped tone pips (gap detection)
Outcome: gap-detection thresholds ~11 ms (infants), 5.6 ms (children), 5.2 ms (adults)
Evidence_Quote: Listeners who were 6.5 months, 12 months, 5 years, and 21 years of age were required to discriminate a pair of 500-Hz, Gaussian-enveloped tone pips from a short 500-Hz tone of the same duration and total energy.

Title: Infants require low-frequency energy to hear the pitch of the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental) with low- or high-frequency energy
Outcome: infants categorize low-frequency (resolvable) complexes by missing-fundamental pitch but fail to categorize high-frequency (unresolvable) complexes
Evidence_Quote: infants first learned to discriminate two harmonic tonal complexes based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: The development of frequency resolution in humans as revealed by the auditory brain-stem response recorded with notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: tone-pip stimuli with notched-noise masking (ABR)
Outcome: 3-month-olds do not have adultlike tuning for 8000 Hz stimulation; tuning-function width is adultlike by 6 months for high- and low-frequency probes
Evidence_Quote: Tone-pip stimuli at 1000, 4000, and 8000 Hz (50 dB nHL) were presented simultaneously with notched-noise masking

Title: Frequency contribution to the click-evoked auditory brain-stem response in human adults and infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli with notched-noise masking (ABR)
Outcome: infants show adultlike latency shifts across notch center frequencies, suggesting mature tonotopic organization by 3 months
Evidence_Quote: when the ABR is recorded in the presence of notched-noise masking with center frequencies ranging from 500-8000 Hz

Title: The postnatal development of frequency-place code and tuning characteristics in the auditory midbrain of the phyllostomid bat, Carollia perspicillata.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborn and developing Carollia perspicillata bats
Stimulus_Type: Acoustic stimulation (characteristic-frequency mapping in inferior colliculus)
Outcome: Hearing range and tonotopy development in the inferior colliculus
Evidence_Quote: The experimental animal, Carollia perspicillata, has an adult hearing range of 7-110 kHz (characteristic frequencies) but lack any significant overrepresentation of a limited frequency band as known for rhinolophoid bats and Pteronotus. The audiogram of the newborn Carollia includes characteristic frequencies from 8 to 76 kHz, which is about 65% of the adult hearing range. As in adults, low frequencies are represented in the dorsolateral portion of the IC. However, at birth the ventromedial IC is non-responsive to acoustic stimulation up to intensities of 90 dB SPL.

Title: The relationship between auditory brainstem response latencies and behavioral thresholds in normal hearing infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Tone pips (ABR latencies and behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: ABR latency-behavioral threshold relationship by age group
Evidence_Quote: The relationship between behavioral thresholds and auditory brainstem response (ABR) latencies for 4 and 8 kHz tone pips were examined in normal-hearing 3-month-olds, 6-month-olds and adults.

Title: Noise induced hearing loss in fetal sheep.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: broadband noise, 120 dB SPL for 16 h (exposure of pregnant ewes); ABR clicks and tone bursts via bone oscillator
Outcome: noise-induced ABR threshold elevation in fetal sheep
Evidence_Quote: The auditory brainstem response (ABR) was recorded in utero from chronically instrumented fetal sheep prior to and following exposure of pregnant ewes to intense broadband noise (120 dB SPL for 16 h). ABRs were elicited by clicks and tone bursts (0.5, 1, 2, and 4 kHz) delivered through a bone oscillator

Title: Changes in the cat cochlear nucleus following neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation; ABR/FFR testing
Outcome: Cochlear nucleus volume, spherical cell size and density after deafening/stimulation
Evidence_Quote: Profound hearing loss was confirmed in each animal by auditory brainstem response (ABR) and frequency following response (500 Hz) testing. Five of the kittens were implanted unilaterally with a scala tympani electrode array at ages 8-16 weeks. These kittens were stimulated daily for four hours at 2 dB above the evoked ABR threshold, over a period of three months, and subsequently euthanized for histological analysis at 26-32 weeks of age.

Title: Recovery of auditory function and structure in the chick after two intense pure tone exposures.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonatal chicks (exposed at 2 or 16 days of age)
Stimulus_Type: Intense pure tone exposure
Outcome: Threshold shift (about 57 dB at 0 days) and cochlear structural recovery after exposure
Evidence_Quote: Groups of neonatal chicks were examined in three experimental conditions that differed in the age and number of times they were exposed to a pure tone of 0.9 kHz at 120 dB SPL for 48 h. Several animals were exposed once at 2 or 16 days of age, while others were subjected twice to the above stimulus, first at 2 days and then at 16 days. Evoked potential measures of threshold shift, obtained at 0, 12 or 26 days post-exposure, were used to determine the degree of hearing loss and recovery. The average threshold loss in the mid-range frequencies was about 57 dB at 0 days for all three conditions.

Title: Pressure transfer function and absorption cross section from the diffuse field to the human infant ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: Diffuse-field pink noise from loudspeaker in reverberant room (ear-canal pressure measurement)
Outcome: Diffuse-field pressure transfer function and absorption cross section vs age
Evidence_Quote: The diffuse-field pressure transfer function from a reverberant field to the ear canal of human infants, ages 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months, has been measured from 125-10700 Hz.

Title: Aspects of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in healthy newborns.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) recorded in ear canal (no applied stimulus)
Outcome: SOAE prevalence 78%; levels -2 to 42 dB SPL; most emissions above 2 kHz
Evidence_Quote: The SOAE levels were between -2 and 42 dB SPL. The mean level per emitting ear was 8.0 dB SPL and not significantly different between right and left ears or genders.

Title: The sensitivity to 3,3'-iminodipropionitrile differs for high- and midfrequency hearing loss in the developing rat.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: 3,3'-iminodipropionitrile (IDPN); 5- and 40-kHz tones
Outcome: auditory thresholds; adult-like IDPN susceptibility reached ~PND 30-32; early exposure caused high-frequency-selective loss
Evidence_Quote: All animals were tested as adults for auditory thresholds to 5- and 40-kHz tones using reflex modification audiometry.

Title: Development of hearing in neonatal rats: air and bone conducted ABR thresholds.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: air-conducted (AC) and bone-conducted (BC) ABR stimuli (levels in dB HL)
Outcome: development of air- and bone-conduction ABR thresholds; air-bone gap resolved by PND 15
Evidence_Quote: ABR to maximal intensity BC stimuli (55 dB above adult rat ABR threshold--55 dB HL*) could be recorded from PND 7-8 while AC responses to 80 dB HL* stimuli, only from PND 11.

Title: The growth of hearing loss in neonatal chicks exposed to intense pure tones.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Intense pure tone exposure; probe tones for tuning curves
Outcome: Threshold shift and tuning sharpness vs exposure duration
Evidence_Quote: One-day-old chicks were exposed to an intense pure tone (0.9 kHz, 120 dB SPL) and assigned to one of eight groups based on continuous exposure durations from 1 to 200 h. As each animal was removed from the exposure, it was anesthetized and an electrode was placed in the nucleus magnocellularis.
