Sound-evoked potentials were used to measure absolute thresholds and frequency selectivity. Thresholds were measured at 10 frequencies between 0.1 and 4.5 kHz while frequency selectivity was assessed by a simultaneous masking tuning-curve procedure at five probe-tone frequencies between 0.3 and 2.5 kHz. Threshold shift was greatest at 1.3 kHz and reached a maximum loss of approximately 57 dB between 48 and 200 h of exposure.

Title: Simultaneous masking in newborn chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Tone masker and signal tones (simultaneous masking)
Outcome: Masking patterns mature at hatching, similar to adult humans
Evidence_Quote: In the first experiment data were collected with a 500-Hz masker presented at 15 or 25 dB above absolute threshold.

Title: Ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient in human infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants of age 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months and adults
Stimulus_Type: Ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient measurement
Outcome: Ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient development
Evidence_Quote: The ear-canal impedance and reflection coefficient were measured in an adult group and in groups of infants of age 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months over frequency range 125-10,700 Hz.

Title: Behavioral measures of auditory thresholds in developing tree shrews (Tupaia belangeri).
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: developing tree shrews (from day 16 after birth to weanlings)
Stimulus_Type: Tones (behavioral threshold testing)
Outcome: Hearing onset (day 18) and auditory threshold development
Evidence_Quote: The development of hearing in tree shrews (Tupaia belangeri) was tested through behavioral measures in the range of 0.3-60 kHz from the first postnatal thresholds detectable through to those of weanlings.

Title: Acoustic impedance of the maternal abdomen.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: nine women during their last trimester of pregnancy
Stimulus_Type: Electromechanical shaker vibrations applied to the maternal abdomen
Outcome: Driving-point impedance of maternal abdomen; resonance at 28 +/- 16 Hz
Evidence_Quote: An electromechanical shaker with a contact area of 2.85 cm2 produced abdominal vibrations between 10 and 500 Hz, and the resulting force and acceleration were measured.

Title: The relationship between auditory brainstem response and behavioral thresholds in normal hearing infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Tone pips (ABR and behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: ABR vs behavioral threshold development and correlation
Evidence_Quote: Thresholds were estimated for tone pips at 1, 4, and 8 kHz, presented at a rate of 13.3/s.

Title: Amplitude-modulation following response (AMFR): effects of modulation rate, carrier frequency, age, and state.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Amplitude-modulated (AM) continuous tones (AMFR)
Outcome: Optimal AM rate 40 Hz in adults, 80 Hz in infants (AMFR coherence)
Evidence_Quote: Stimulus AM rate was varied between 10 and 80 Hz for continuous tonal stimuli of 500 Hz, and between 20 and 80 Hz for continuous tonal stimuli of 2000 Hz.

Title: Critical ages in brainstem development revealed by neonatal 3-channel Lissajous' trajectory of auditory brainstem evoked potentials.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Clicks (auditory brainstem evoked potentials, 3CLT)
Outcome: ABEP/3CLT descriptors vs gestational age, stimulus intensity and rate
Evidence_Quote: ABEPs were evoked by alternating polarity, monaural 75 dBnHL clicks presented at rates of 10/s, 55/s and 80/s. Potentials were also recorded to 45 dBnHL and 15 dBnHL clicks presented at 10/s.

Title: Tectorial membrane regeneration in acoustically damaged birds: an immunocytochemical technique.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: octave band noise, center frequency 1.5 kHz, for 4 h
Outcome: tectorial membrane regeneration after acoustic damage
Evidence_Quote: Birds were exposed to an octave band noise with a center frequency of 1.5 kHz at 116 dB SPL for 4 h.

Title: Decreased cardiac responses to auditory stimulation during prone sleep.
Journal: Pediatrics
Target_Age: healthy infants, median age 11 weeks (30 studied, 20 analyzed)
Stimulus_Type: white-noise auditory stimulation during sleep
Outcome: auditory challenge induces smaller cardiac responses in prone than in supine sleep
Evidence_Quote: Their behavioral and cardiac responses were recorded during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, both before and after exposure to 90 dB (A) of white-noise.

Title: Coherence analysis of envelope-following responses (EFRs) and frequency-following responses (FFRs) in infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: Amplitude-modulated (AM) tones (EFR/FFR stimuli)
Outcome: EFR/FFR coherence growth and thresholds compared between infants and adults
Evidence_Quote: A modulation frequency of 80 Hz was used in infants; modulation frequencies of 40 and 80 Hz were used in adults.

Title: Estimating the contribution of non-sensory factors to infant-adult differences in behavioral thresholds.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: infants 8 to 11 months old and adults
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz tone in quiet and in masking noise (behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: Infant-adult threshold difference 12 dB; minimum masking level difference 8 dB
Evidence_Quote: In this investigation, thresholds in quiet and in increasing levels of a masking noise for a 1 kHz tone, in infants 8 to 11 months old and in adults, were determined.

Title: Ontogeny of hearing in the marsupial, Monodelphis domestica, as revealed by brainstem auditory evoked potentials.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: Brazilian short-tailed opossum (Monodelphis domestica), from 29 days after birth
Stimulus_Type: brainstem auditory evoked potential (BAEP) stimuli
Outcome: ontogeny of hearing range and thresholds
Evidence_Quote: The hearing range at the onset of hearing is limited to 5-20 kHz with lowest thresholds of 60 dB SPL at 8-12 kHz.

Title: The cochlear place-frequency map of the adult and developing Mongolian gerbil.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: adult and subadult (18 days after birth) Mongolian gerbils
Stimulus_Type: physiological characterization of single auditory nerve fibers (place-frequency map)
Outcome: cochlear place-frequency map and its maturational shift
Evidence_Quote: The map was established for frequencies between 0.3 and 31.9 kHz. As in other mammals, a baso-apical frequency gradient from high to low frequencies was found. The slope of the place-frequency map amounted to 1.5 mm/octave for higher frequencies. Below 4 kHz the slope decreased to a value of 1 mm/octave at 0.5 kHz. A shift in the frequency map occurs during cochlear maturation. The place-frequency map in subadult gerbils (18 days after birth) is shifted by a distance corresponding to an octave, at least for frequencies above 6 kHz.

Title: Thyroxine affects physiological and morphological development of the ear.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPE) and ABR clicks; stimulus intensities 50 and 70 dB SPL
Outcome: effect of thyroxine on onset/development of DPE, ABR and ear morphology
Evidence_Quote: DPEs were recorded at an earlier postnatal age to high (8 kHz) frequencies and progressed to lower (3 kHz) frequencies with age. ABRs to high-intensity clicks were recorded at least 2 days before DPEs, although DPE onset at 8 kHz preceded adult-like ABR thresholds. Both ABR and DPEs appeared earlier in the hyperthyroid rats. Histological evidence showed earlier morphological development of the ear in these animals. ABR thresholds and DPE amplitudes matured at a slower rate in the experimental group despite their earlier onset. There was no difference in ABR and DPE thresholds between adult hyperthyroid and control rats. However, in the experimental group, DPEs had smaller amplitudes to high (70 dB SPL) and to low (50 dB SPL) stimulus intensities at low frequencies.

Title: Anatomical correlates of the passive properties underlying the developmental shift in the frequency map of the mammalian cochlea.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: none (cochlear morphology measurements)
Outcome: basilar membrane dimensions do not change as the place code shifts; organ of Corti size and basilar membrane fiber-band thickness do
Evidence_Quote: regions that code for the roughly the same frequency (e.g., approximately 11.2 kHz) at different ages can have basilar membranes of very different dimensions

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning curves in human adults and neonates.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 15 normal-hearing adults and 16 healthy term-born neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with suppressor tone (iso-suppression tuning curves)
Outcome: DPOAE STCs stable with tip centered at f2; neonatal STCs at 3000 and 6000 Hz comparable to adults, suggesting mature cochlear tuning by term birth
Evidence_Quote: The 2f1-f2 DPOAE was elicited using f2/f1 = 1.2, LI = 1.2, LI = 65 and L2 = 50 dB SPL. A suppressor tone was presented at frequencies ranging from 1 octave below to 1/4 octave above f2 and varied in level until DPOAE amplitude was reduced by 6 dB. The suppressor level required for 6 dB suppression was plotted as function of suppressor frequency to generate a DPOAE STC. Forward-masked psychoacoustic tuning curves (PTC) were obtained for three of the adult subjects. Results indicate that DPOAE STCs are stable and show minimal inter- and intra-subject variability. The tip of the STC is consistently centered around the f2 region and STCs are similar in shape, width (Q10) and slope to VIIIth-nerve TCs. PTCs and STCs measured in the same subject showed similar trends, although PTCs had narrower width and steeper slope. Neonatal STCs were recorded at 3000 and 6000 Hz only

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) amplitude as a function of f2/f1 frequency ratio and primary tone level separation in human adults and neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2/f1 ratio and primary level separation varied)
Outcome: optimal f2/f1 ratio comparable in adults and neonates; 10-15 dB level separation optimal in adults and term neonates but not premature neonates
Evidence_Quote: Two f2 frequencies were investigated: 1500 and 6000 Hz.

Title: The effect of the evanescent wave upon acoustic measurements in the human ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no participants (theoretical predictions for human adults and 1-month-old infants)
Stimulus_Type: none (theoretical model of ear-canal acoustic measurement)
Outcome: evanescent-wave error below 10 kHz predicted at 3 dB in adults and 1.3 dB in 1-month-old infants
Evidence_Quote: The maximum measurement error due to the presence of the evanescent wave in human ear canals below 10 kHz is predicted to be 3 dB in adults and 1.3 dB in 1 month old infants, when the loudspeaker and microphone ports are spaced more than 2 mm apart.

Title: Auditory threshold sensitivity of the human neonate as measured by the auditory brainstem response.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: healthy, full-term human neonates and young adults
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone-bursts of 0.5, 1.5, 4.0 and 8.0 kHz embedded in notched noise (ABR)
Outcome: infant ABR thresholds elevated by 3-25 dB relative to adult thresholds, greatest for high-frequency stimuli
Evidence_Quote: ABRs were elicited with clicks and tone-bursts of 0.5, 1.5, 4.0 and 8.0 kHz, embedded in notched noise, in healthy, full-term human neonates

Title: Anatomy of the normal human cochlear aqueduct with functional implications.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 101 human temporal bones, ages 0-100 years (19 aged 0-1 years)
Stimulus_Type: none (temporal-bone anatomy; quantitative model of aqueduct function)
Outcome: aqueduct patency types and dimensions described; model suggests little effect on sound transmission above 20 Hz in normal ears
Evidence_Quote: has little effect on normal ossicular transmission of sound for frequencies above 20 Hz. In pathological ears, such as those with ossicular disruption or after a type IV tympanoplasty, a patent aqueduct might affect hearing for frequencies below 150 Hz.

Title: Features of the auditory development of the short-tailed Brazilian opossum, Monodelphis domestica: evoked responses, neonatal vocalizations and synapses in the inferior colliculus.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: short-tailed Brazilian opossum (Monodelphis domestica) pups, postnatal days 24-40
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli (evoked potentials); pup isolation calls
Outcome: hearing onset at postnatal day 24 with threshold 83 dB SPL, declining below 58 dB by day 40; isolation call peaks near 13 kHz
Evidence_Quote: Evoked potentials were first recorded at postnatal day 24 at a threshold of 83 dB SPL; thresholds declined over subsequent weeks to below 58 dB at 40 days. Isolation calls emitted by the pups had stereotypic spectra with peaks at near 13 kHz and an octave higher.

Title: Cochlear pathology induced by aminoglycoside ototoxicity during postnatal maturation in cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: none (neomycin administration; cochlear histology)
Outcome: hair cell degeneration progresses from base to apex; spiral ganglion loss in the middle cochlea (approximately 2.8-8 kHz) is independent of hair cell loss
Evidence_Quote: with initial cell loss occurring in the middle of the cochlea, about 40-60% from the base (approximately 2.8-8 kHz)

Title: Temporary threshold shifts induced by low-pass and high-pass filtered noises in fetal sheep in utero.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: low-pass and high-pass filtered noise (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz), approx. 120 dB SPL, 16 h
Outcome: temporary ABR threshold shifts after filtered-noise exposure
Evidence_Quote: Auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) were obtained from nine late gestational age fetal sheep in utero before and after a 16-h exposure to low-pass (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz) and high-pass (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz) noises (approximately 120 dB sound pressure level, recorded in air). Bone-conduction ABRs were elicited by broadband clicks and 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 kHz tone bursts.

Title: Infants' pitch perception: masking by low- and high-frequency noises.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones and harmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental), presented with low- or high-frequency noise
Outcome: infants discriminate pure tones in high-frequency noise but not low-frequency noise, and categorize missing-fundamental complexes like adults, indicating central pitch processing
Evidence_Quote: Adults and infants were presented with either pure tones of 160 and 200 Hz or harmonic tonal complexes with pitches equivalent to 160 and 200 Hz.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions in human newborns and adults. I. Frequency effects.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human newborns (term and preterm) and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (varied f2)
Outcome: newborns have larger 2 f1-f2 DPOAE amplitudes than adults at lower f2; similar amplitudes at the highest f2 assessed
Evidence_Quote: At the highest frequencies assessed (f2 = 4.2-9.9 kHz) all subjects had similar amplitude 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs. At lower frequencies adult 2 f1-f2 amplitudes were significantly less than those of newborns. At the lowest frequencies reliably assessed (f2 = 1.5-2.1 kHz) term newborns had significantly larger 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs than preterm newborns.

Title: Development of auditory function in the tammar wallaby Macropus eugenii.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: developing tammar wallabies (pouch young, ~95 to >180 days)
Stimulus_Type: click and tone burst stimuli (bone and air conduction) for ABR
Outcome: development of ABR thresholds and latencies
Evidence_Quote: Thresholds to tone bursts in the centre frequency range (4-12 kHz) remained less than those for low (0.5-1.5 kHz) and higher (16 kHz) frequencies.

Title: A developmental study of distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) suppression in humans.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 14 normal-hearing adults, 33 term and 85 premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (suppression tuning curves)
Outcome: premature neonates show narrower STCs and atypical suppression growth at f2 of 1500 and 6000 Hz, indicating immature cochlear frequency resolution
Evidence_Quote: Premature neonates showed non-adult-like DPOAE suppression at f2 of 1500 and 6000 Hz

Title: Gender distinctions and lateral asymmetry in the low-level auditory brainstem response of the human neonate.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone-burst stimuli (ABR)
Outcome: male infants have lower ABR thresholds than females (right-ear difference 7.45 dB, left-ear 1.56 dB); right-ear advantage in wave V amplitude
Evidence_Quote: Threshold measures of auditory brainstem response (ABR) were generated in 72 full-term newborn infants in response to clicks and tone burst stimuli between 500 and 8000 Hz as detailed in a previous study.

Title: Postnatal development of the organ of Corti in cats: a light microscopic morphometric study.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: kittens (P1, P5, P10, P15) and adult cats
Stimulus_Type: none (morphometric study; cochlear place best frequencies)
Outcome: postnatal development of organ of Corti morphology
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made of the organ of Corti at 3 cochlear locations: 20%, 60% and 85% of basilar membrane length from the base cochlear locations which in the adult correspond to best frequencies of approximately 20 kHz, 2 kHz and 500 Hz, respectively. In addition, measurements of basilar membrane length and opening of the tunnel of Corti were made in 20 cochlear specimens from kittens aged P0-P6. Results indicate that: (i) at P0 the basilar membrane has attained adult length, and the tunnel of Corti is open over approximately the basal one-half of the cochlea; (ii) the initial opening of the tunnel of Corti occurs at a site about 4 mm from the cochlear base (best frequency of approximately 25 kHz in the adult cochlea)
